literal: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian
idiomatic: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian

literal: Yu Jin, styled Anren.
idiomatic: Yu Jin, styled Anren.

literal: His father Qingbin was Wei governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: His father Qingbin had been Wei governor of Sizhou.

literal: Jin from youth was quick and perceptive, loved learning, and admired goodness.
idiomatic: From youth Jin was quick-witted, loved study, and sought what was good.

literal: He was gradually promoted to straight attendant.
idiomatic: He rose in turn to straight attendant.

literal: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin took his maternal niece, daughter of the Pi clan, and was thereby promoted and appointed secretariat vice-director.
idiomatic: When Sima Ziru held power, Jin married his maternal niece of the Pi clan and was promoted secretariat vice-director.

literal: Being Ziru's affinal kin, he often went to call on him and thereby came to be on easy terms with eminent predecessors and noted men of the age.
idiomatic: As Ziru's kin by marriage he often called on him and grew familiar with eminent elders and men of name.

literal: When Gao Cheng entered the court, Jin was ordered to be at Ye's northern palace together with Gao Dezheng managing confidential affairs.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng came to court, Jin was ordered to Ye's northern palace to manage confidential affairs with Gao Dezheng.

literal: When Gao Yan assisted in government, Jin was repeatedly promoted to minister of personnel.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan assisted in government, Jin rose repeatedly to minister of personnel.

literal: When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been a guest-officer of Ziru, Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old acquaintances from the imperial hometown, and they jointly recommended and advanced him; his appointment and favor grew ever heavier.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhan took the throne, Zhao Yanshen had been Ziru's guest-officer, and Yuan Wenyao and He Shikai were all old friends from the imperial hometown. They recommended him together, and his rank and favor grew heavier still.

literal: Moreover the personnel directorate's weighing and selection fell to him; affairs were mostly secret, and thereby he often heard beforehand of the court's weighty matters.
idiomatic: Personnel weighing and selection also rested with him; much was secret, and so he often heard the court's weighty affairs in advance.

literal: Soon he was additionally right vice director, acting in selection; before long he received the formal appointment.
idiomatic: Soon he was also right vice director, acting in selection; before long the post was made formal.

literal: He died of illness; Gao Zhan was at the time drinking at Santai; Wenyao reported it, and the emperor ordered music withdrawn and drinking stopped.
idiomatic: He died of illness while Gao Zhan was drinking at Santai. Wenyao reported it, and the emperor ordered the music stopped and the drinking ended.

literal: Outwardly Jin was prominent, but inwardly his household lacked moral instruction; his inner chambers were foul and mixed, and the age despised him for it.
idiomatic: Outwardly Jin was eminent, but at home he lacked moral discipline; his inner quarters were foul and disorderly, and the age despised him.

literal: Yet he could also restrain himself and defer to scholars, meaning to draw in eminent men—but he did not distinguish them.
idiomatic: Yet he could humble himself before scholars and meant to draw in men of name—only he could not tell them apart.

literal: When his office was high and his burden heavy, he became greatly impatient; within the ministry, those lang who wished to discuss affairs—if they went against him he would glare and curse at once, and they could not consult with him.
idiomatic: Once rank and burden grew heavy he turned harsh and quick to anger. Within the ministry, any lang who came to discuss business and crossed him was glared at and cursed on the spot; none could seek his counsel.

literal: Once he held the great selection, he became all the more arrogant and harsh.
idiomatic: Once he held the great selection he grew still more arrogant and cruel.

literal: His son Dezai succeeded him.
idiomatic: His son Dezai succeeded him.

literal: Feng Zicong, a man of Xindu, was a descendant of Northern Yan's ruler Feng Ba.
idiomatic: Feng Zicong came from Xindu and was descended from Northern Yan's ruler Feng Ba.

literal: His father Lingshao was a lang in the revenue section.
idiomatic: His father Lingshao was a lang in the revenue section.

literal: Zicong was clever by nature and ranged through books and records.
idiomatic: Zicong was clever by nature and read widely in books and records.

literal: He took office.
idiomatic: He then entered official service.

literal: Gao Yan appointed him to the staff bureau for law in the general-in-chief's office, managing confidential affairs and acting in the treasury section.
idiomatic: Gao Yan made him law staff in the general-in-chief's office, put him in charge of confidential affairs, and had him act in the treasury section.

literal: Gao Yan once reviewed ledgers; testing them, he had Zicong recite orally—and Zicong answered from memory without a single omission.
idiomatic: Gao Yan once reviewed ledgers and tested Zicong by having him recite them aloud. Zicong answered from memory without missing a single entry.

literal: Zicong's wife was the younger sister of the Hu empress.
idiomatic: Zicong's wife was the Hu empress's younger sister.

literal: He was promoted to attendant within the palace and additionally made eastern palace recorder.
idiomatic: He was promoted palace attendant and also made eastern palace recorder.

literal: He was further given a separate edict to assist the crown prince together with Hu Changcai; he was transferred to subprefect of the heir apparent.
idiomatic: By a separate edict he was to assist the crown prince with Hu Changcai and was transferred to heir-apparent subprefect.

literal: When Gao Zhan died, Vice Director He Shikai had long attended his illness and kept the mourning secret for three days without announcing it.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhan died, vice director He Shikai had long attended his illness and kept the mourning secret for three days without announcing it.

literal: Zicong asked He Shikai why he did not announce the mourning.
idiomatic: Zicong asked He Shikai why he had not announced the mourning.

literal: He Shikai cited that when Gao Huan and Gao Cheng first died, mourning was likewise kept secret; the sovereign was young and he feared the princes and dukes might harbor divided hearts; he intended to summon everyone to the Cool Breeze Hall and then discuss in detail.
idiomatic: He Shikai said that when Gao Huan and Gao Cheng first died, mourning had likewise been kept secret. The sovereign was young; he feared the princes and dukes might waver, and meant to gather everyone at the Cool Breeze Hall before discussing matters in full.

literal: At the time Grand Mentor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs Prince of Zhao commandery Rui had long dwelt within the palace and took part in counsel at the curtain; Zicong had long known He Shikai resented Rui and General-in-Chief of the Guards Prince of Huai'nan Lou Dingyuan, and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on external appointment and strip Dingyuan of guard authority; therefore he answered, saying, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign likewise received the throne from the former emperor. Every minister's wealth and rank came from father and son's grace to the sovereign. If the honored men within the court are left wholly unchanged, the princes and dukes below will surely harbor no other intent.
idiomatic: At the time grand mentor and recorder of the masters of writing affairs, Prince of Zhao commandery Rui, had long lived inside the palace and shared counsel at the curtain. Zicong knew He Shikai resented Rui and general-in-chief of the guards Prince of Huai'nan Lou Dingyuan and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on provincial duty and strip Dingyuan of the guard command. He answered, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign too received the throne from his predecessor. Every minister's wealth came from the sovereign father and son. Leave the great men inside the court unchanged, and the princes and dukes below will surely have no other wish.

literal: Times and affairs differ; this cannot be compared with the founding reign.
idiomatic: "Times and affairs differ; this cannot be compared with the founding reign.

literal: Moreover, sir, you have been outside the palace gates already several days; news of the emperor's passing spreads on every road. If mourning is long delayed, I fear some other change may arise.
idiomatic: "Moreover, sir, you have been outside the palace gates for days already, and news of the emperor's passing travels every road. Delay mourning too long and I fear some other turn may come.

literal: " Thereupon mourning was announced.
idiomatic: " Thereupon mourning was announced.

literal: Yuan Wenyao, because Zicong was the empress's brother-in-law, feared he would encourage the empress to meddle in government; he persuaded Prince of Zhao commandery and He Shikai to send him out, appointed him governor of Zhengzhou, and ordered him to take up the post at once.
idiomatic: Yuan Wenyao, because Zicong was the empress's brother-in-law, feared he would encourage her to meddle in government. He persuaded Prince of Zhao commandery and He Shikai to send him out, made him governor of Zheng, and ordered him to take up the post at once.

literal: Zicong's appointment to the province was not the Later Sovereign's original intent; the central edict was earnest and warm, and he was specially given rear guard musicians, fifty additional troops, and permission to bring goods across the passes.
idiomatic: Zicong's provincial appointment was not what the Later Sovereign had first intended; the central edict was warm and earnest, and he was specially given rear guard musicians, fifty more troops, and leave to bring goods across the passes.

literal: Not long after he reached the province, the empress dowager took Zicong's eldest daughter as consort for Prince of Qi'an; Zicong therefore asked leave to go to Ye and was then appointed minister of personnel.
idiomatic: Not long after he reached the province, the empress dowager took Zicong's eldest daughter as consort for Prince of Qi'an. Zicong asked leave to go to Ye and was then made minister of personnel.

literal: His wife relied on kinship and acted without restraint; requests and audiences went openly, and bribes piled up.
idiomatic: His wife relied on kinship and acted without restraint; favors and audiences went openly, and bribes piled high.

literal: When prefects and magistrates were appointed, the amount of cash and silk was fixed first and only then reported to the throne; whatever they sought through him was never denied, and Zicong did not restrain it.
idiomatic: For prefects and magistrates the price in cash and silk was fixed first and only then reported upward. Whatever they sought through him was granted, and Zicong did not restrain them.

literal: Before long he was promoted to right vice director of the masters of writing and still acted in selection.
idiomatic: Before long he was promoted right vice director of the masters of writing and still acted in selection.

literal: He Shikai had long held a key post; Zicong had once relied on him and with humble words and bent body consulted him on every matter.
idiomatic: He Shikai had long held power; Zicong had once relied on him, spoke humbly, bowed low, and consulted him on every matter.

literal: He Shikai's younger brother Xiu married into the Lu clan; Zicong attended and hurried about no differently from He Shikai's staff.
idiomatic: He Shikai's younger brother Xiu married into the Lu clan; Zicong hurried about at the wedding no differently from He Shikai's own staff.

literal: At the time many inner appointments were proposed by He Shikai; Zicong, relying on inner kinship and also holding the selection office, monopolized favor and power, and friction arose.
idiomatic: At the time many inner appointments came from He Shikai's proposals. Zicong, relying on inner kinship and also holding the selection office, monopolized favor and power, and friction grew between them.

literal: Prince of Langye Yan killed He Shikai; Zicong took part in the affair and strangled him inside the inner secretariat.
idiomatic: Prince of Langye Yan killed He Shikai; Zicong took part in the affair and strangled him inside the inner secretariat.

literal: Zicong had some discernment, but as rank and renown rose his long-held intent suddenly changed.
idiomatic: Zicong had some discernment, but as rank and renown rose his old intent suddenly changed.

literal: He promoted and drew in unworthy sorts and treated them as close friends;
idiomatic: He promoted unworthy men and treated them as close friends;

literal: he indulged his sons and younger brothers, giving offices out of proper order;
idiomatic: he indulged his sons and younger brothers, giving offices out of proper order;

literal: he also specialized in arranging marriages, choosing only great houses, and routinely promised office and rank; within ten days it was confirmed.
idiomatic: he also specialized in arranging marriages, choosing only great houses, and routinely promised office and rank that were confirmed within ten days.

literal: His son Cizheng.
idiomatic: His son was Cizheng.

literal: Helian Ziyue, styled Shixin, was a descendant of Helian Bobo.
idiomatic: Helian Ziyue, styled Shixin, was descended from Helian Bobo.

literal: In the first year of Yong'an under Wei he was made, for military merit, separate-assistant of Jizhou.
idiomatic: In Wei's first Yong'an year he was made Jizhou separate-assistant for military merit.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous army, Hou Jing was governor; Jing had originally been Erzhu Rong's trusted man, and Ziyue urged Jing to join the uprising; Jing followed him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous army, Hou Jing was governor. Jing had been Erzhu Rong's trusted man; Ziyue urged him to join the uprising, and Jing followed.

literal: He was appointed defender of Linyu.
idiomatic: He was appointed defender of Linyu.

literal: Gao Cheng was going to Jinyang and passed through that commandery; he therefore asked what was inconvenient.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng was bound for Jinyang and passed through the commandery, so he asked what was inconvenient.

literal: Ziyue answered, saying, "The two counties of Linshui and Wu'an lie far from the commandery seat; mountains and ridges overlap, and cart and foot travel are hard. If they were attached east to Wei's commandery, the land would be level and the road near.
idiomatic: Ziyue answered, "The counties of Linshui and Wu'an lie far from the seat; mountains pile up and travel by cart or on foot is hard. If they were placed under Wei's commandery to the east, the land would be level and the road short.

literal: " Gao Cheng laughed and said, "You only know how to benefit the people and do not notice the harm to the trunk.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng laughed and said, "You only know how to ease the people and do not see the harm to the trunk.

literal: Ziyue answered, saying, "What I spoke of follows the people's hardship; I dare not let private gain outweigh my heart.
idiomatic: Ziyue answered, "What I said follows the people's hardship; I dare not let private gain outweigh my heart.

literal: " Gao Cheng said, "You can be like this—very good, very good.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng said, "You can be like this—excellent, excellent.

literal: " He then ordered it carried out according to the proposal.
idiomatic: " He then ordered the change carried out as proposed.

literal: When his term in the commandery was complete, he was summoned again as magistrate of Linzhang.
idiomatic: When his commandery term ended he was summoned again as magistrate of Linzhang.

literal: Later he was made governor of Zhengzhou; at the time the region had just suffered the great flood of the Heqing era, and the people had fled in great numbers; Ziyue personally went to comfort and shelter them, households increased, and his governance ranked first in the realm.
idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Zheng. The region had just suffered the Heqing great flood; many people had fled. Ziyue went in person to comfort them, households increased, and his governance ranked first in the realm.

literal: He entered court as director of the ministry of justice; more than eight hundred men of Zhengzhou asked to erect a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.
idiomatic: He entered court as director of the ministry of justice. More than eight hundred men of Zheng asked to raise a stele praising his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

literal: Later, in his original office, he was additionally made acting in the personnel directorate.
idiomatic: Later, while keeping his original office, he was additionally made acting in the personnel directorate.

literal: Ziyue in office relied only on purity and diligence to hold himself; he had neither learning nor bearing, and in human discernment he fell ever farther away—yet once he stood at the head of weighing and selection, he drew great criticism from the age.
idiomatic: In office Ziyue held himself only by purity and diligence. He had neither learning nor bearing, and in judging men he fell ever farther short—yet once he stood at the head of weighing and selection, he drew heavy criticism.

literal: Thereupon he was made director of the ministry of rites and died.
idiomatic: Thereupon he was made director of the ministry of rites and died.

literal: Tang Yong, styled Daohe, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan; his ancestors had moved there from Jinchang.
idiomatic: Tang Yong, styled Daohe, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan; his ancestors had moved there from Jinchang.

literal: His father Lingzhi was Wei magistrate of Shouyang.
idiomatic: His father Lingzhi was Wei magistrate of Shouyang.

literal: Yong from youth was bright and keen and had the talent and equipment to order an age.
idiomatic: Yong was bright and keen from youth and had the talent to order an age.

literal: In the first year of Taichang someone recommended him to Gao Huan; Gao Huan ordered him to attend the outer military affairs bureau and manage written registers.
idiomatic: In the first Taichang year someone recommended him to Gao Huan, who had him attend the outer military affairs bureau and manage written registers.

literal: Yong was skilled at reckoning and accounts, had a strong memory and silent retention, and was known for practical ability; he was promoted staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's office.
idiomatic: Yong was skilled at reckoning and accounts, remembered silently, and was known for practical ability. He was promoted staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's office.

literal: When Gao Cheng died, affairs arose in sudden haste; Gao Yang deployed the generals and soldiers and suppressed the four quarters; in the night he summoned Yong to arrange matters, and at once it was done—Gao Yang valued him greatly.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng died, affairs broke out in haste. Gao Yang deployed generals and soldiers to hold the four quarters, summoned Yong at night to arrange matters, and at once it was done. Gao Yang valued him greatly.

literal: Gao Yang year after year went beyond the frontier; Yong always accompanied him and specialized in military plans.
idiomatic: Year after year Gao Yang went beyond the frontier; Yong always accompanied him and specialized in military plans.

literal: His discernment was clear and unhurried, his reception quick; from supervising generals down, and military clerks and above, merit and service followed the thread and none was unfamiliar—whenever there was inquiry, his reply came like an echo.
idiomatic: His discernment was clear and unhurried, his reception quick. From supervising generals down and army clerks up, merit and service followed the thread and none was unfamiliar; whenever he was asked, he answered like an echo.

literal: Sometimes before the emperor he would review troops; though three to five thousand men, Yong often held no ledger and would recite in the dark their offices, ranks, and names, and never erred.
idiomatic: Sometimes the emperor reviewed troops before him; though three or five thousand men, Yong often held no ledger and recited office, rank, and name from memory without error.

literal: In the seventh year, at the Yangfen embankment he lectured on military affairs and ordered Yong to command the discipline of all armies.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, at the Yangfen embankment, he lectured on military affairs and ordered Yong to command discipline for all armies.

literal: When the affair was finished, he still oversaw the ritual of the review feast and archery.
idiomatic: When the affair ended he still oversaw the review feast and archery ritual.

literal: That day Gao Yang personally took Yong's hand, led him before the empress dowager, seated him above Chancellor Hulü Jin, and told the empress dowager, saying, "Tang Yong is strong and capable—one man equals a thousand.
idiomatic: That day Gao Yang took Yong's hand, led him before the empress dowager, seated him above chancellor Hulü Jin, and told her, "Tang Yong is strong and capable—one man equals a thousand.

literal: " He then separately bestowed brocade, silk, cash, and goods.
idiomatic: " He then separately bestowed brocade, silk, cash, and goods.

literal: Yong was not only strong, capable, bright, and discerning; he also knew how to gauge the sovereign's intent, and his paths of advancement were many—therefore favor daily grew and commission grew ever heavier.
idiomatic: Yong was not only strong, capable, bright, and discerning; he also knew how to read the sovereign's intent and had many paths of advance, so favor grew daily and commission grew heavier.

literal: Gao Yang also once said to Yong before the empress dowager, "Tang Yong distinguishes clearly and remembers strongly; whenever there is a weighty military affair, he writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ear at the same time—truly a different man.
idiomatic: Gao Yang also once told the empress dowager before Yong, "Tang Yong distinguishes clearly and remembers strongly. On great military affairs he writes documents by hand, gives orders by mouth, and listens with his ear at once—truly a different man.

literal: " In a single day he was six times given gifts.
idiomatic: " In a single day he was given gifts six times.

literal: He also once removed the blue sable fur coat he was wearing and bestowed it on Yong, saying, "My intent is that carriages, horses, clothes, and furs be worn out together with you.
idiomatic: He also once removed the blue sable coat he was wearing and gave it to Yong, saying, "My intent is that carriages, horses, clothes, and furs be worn out together with you.

literal: " In the tenth year, accompanying the imperial progress to Jinyang, he was made acting attendant of the yellow gate and leading secretariat vice-director.
idiomatic: " In the tenth year, on the progress to Jinyang, Yong was made acting attendant of the yellow gate and leading secretariat vice-director.

literal: Gao Yang once ascended the Tongzi Buddhist temple, looked toward Bingzhou city, and said, "What sort of city is this?
idiomatic: Gao Yang once climbed Tongzi Buddhist temple, looked toward Bingzhou city, and said, "What sort of city is this?

literal: " Someone said, "This is a metal rampart and boiling moat, a realm of heaven's storehouse.
idiomatic: " Someone said, "This is a metal rampart and boiling moat—the realm's heavenly storehouse.

literal: " The emperor said, "I say Tang Yong is the metal rampart; this is not the metal rampart.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I say Tang Yong is the metal rampart; this is not the metal rampart.

literal: " Such was the weight in which he was held.
idiomatic: " Such was the weight in which he was held.

literal: Afterward he said to Yong, "Your toil has been long; I wished to make you governor of a province and repeatedly ordered Yang Zunyan to find another man who could replace you.
idiomatic: Afterward he said to Yong, "Your toil has been long. I wished to make you governor of a province and repeatedly ordered Yang Zunyan to find another man who could replace you.

literal: Zunyan said that having searched everywhere among civil and military men, men like you truly cannot be obtained, and so this intent was stopped.
idiomatic: Zunyan said that having searched civil and military men everywhere, a man like you truly cannot be found, and so this intent was stopped.

literal: You should strive on.
idiomatic: You should strive on.

literal: Gao Yang sometimes sharply rebuked attending ministers who did not suit his intent: "Watch how you comport yourselves—you are not fit to be Tang Yong's slaves.
idiomatic: Gao Yang sometimes sharply rebuked attending ministers who missed his intent: "Watch how you comport yourselves—you are not fit to be Tang Yong's slaves.

literal: " His favor and treatment were mostly of this sort.
idiomatic: " His favor and treatment were mostly of this sort.

literal: When Gao Yan was made chief minister, Yong was made attendant of the yellow gate.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan was made chief minister, Yong was made attendant of the yellow gate.

literal: At the Hualin Garden archery review he was specially given five hundred kinds of gold belts, precious vessels, robes, playthings, and miscellaneous goods.
idiomatic: At the Hualin Garden archery review he was specially given five hundred kinds of gold belts, precious vessels, robes, playthings, and miscellaneous goods.

literal: Early in Tiantong he was made regular attendant and great rectifier of Bingzhou, and again appointed general of the guards; the rest of his offices remained as before.
idiomatic: Early in Tiantong he was made regular attendant and great rectifier of Bing, and again appointed general of the guards; the rest of his offices remained as before.

literal: Yong, because military and civilian instruction in field hunts followed the statute of the twelfth month with three hunts each month, thought men and horses were worn out and memorialized asking for two hunts each month.
idiomatic: Yong thought military and civilian field-hunt instruction, which by statute ran three hunts each month in the twelfth month, wore out men and horses, and memorialized for two hunts each month.

literal: Gao Zhan followed it.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan approved it.

literal: Later he went out as governor of Zhao province; his other offices remained as before.
idiomatic: Later he went out as governor of Zhao; his other offices remained as before.

literal: Gao Zhan said to Yong, "No court minister has yet held regular attendant, general of the guards, and great rectifier while serving as governor; this appointment is because of you. I give you more than a hundred days' rest; in autumn I shall recall you at once.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan said to Yong, "No court minister has yet held regular attendant, general of the guards, and great rectifier while serving as governor; this move is because of you. I give you more than a hundred days' rest; in autumn I shall recall you at once.

literal: He was transferred to right vice director, then again to director of the masters of writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinchang, and made recorder of the masters of writing affairs.
idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice director, then again to director of the masters of writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinchang, and made recorder of the masters of writing affairs.
